summary: Native addon exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials to oob.s4yhii.com on require
details: @galicia-toolkit-nestjs-20-lite/archetype ships only index.js and a prebuilt linux-x64/metrics.node native addon. On module require, index.js unconditionally loads prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node, which reads a broad set of cloud and CI credential environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN) along with hostname, username, and cwd, and POSTs them as JSON to oob.s4yhii.com at path /native. The addon avoids Node's networking APIs: it links fork/setsid/socket/connect/gethostbyname directly and hand-builds a 'POST /native HTTP/1.0' request over a raw socket, daemonizing itself to detach from the parent Node process. The package ships no native source, no binding.gyp, and no publisher-aligned release URL — the entire executable payload is opaque and runs in the installer's Node process on first require. The scope name resembles a NestJS toolkit, but the package exposes no toolkit code; its sole observable behavior on load is credential exfiltration to an attacker-controlled host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
